key_insight: A feedforward neural network trained on the writhe density matrix can classify the first six prime two-component links with very high accuracy, indicating that writhe encodes topology-relevant features.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast, data-driven route for identifying link topology in polymer, DNA, and protein systems where exact topological calculations are computationally expensive.
method: Computed writhe density matrices for thermally equilibrated link configurations
Trained a feedforward neural network to map writhe features to link classes
Tested robustness across temperature, component length, and added Gaussian noise
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97% accuracy on the first six prime links and stayed accurate across temperatures and lengths, but performance dropped sharply when topology-altering Gaussian noise was added.
watch_item: The approach may be sensitive to noise that changes topology, so robustness and generalization to more complex multi-component links need careful validation.
paper_title: Writhe-Based Polymer Link Classification Using Machine Learning
